must_fix.issue: The draft never says what the Wedded Advisor actually does versus what the couple does. Readers picture themselves booking Rome or Milan, hunting a tabaccaio and finding an interpreter alone, and 'finding the interpreter is up to you' (Ceremony and interpreter section) reads as an accountability gap: 'If we're paying a company to organise this, I'd expect them to find the interpreter.' Raised by the primary persona (medium, three times) plus funding_parent (lost_trust, accountability) and uhnw.
must_fix.fix: Reword line 106 so 'up to you' is about the comune, not the couple: e.g. 'Bagno a Ripoli does not provide one, so you bring your own.' (fact_31). Then add 2 to 3 sentences, once, near the timeline or in the close, stating what Wedded Concierge does using brand-facts claims only: one Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments; contracts and holds suppliers; the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins; someone on the ground looks after the days that matter. Also state the sourced fact that each Australian signs the Nulla Osta in person in Rome or Milan and both partners attend the Atto Notorio with the witnesses (fact_06, fact_17), so readers know which steps are theirs. Do NOT claim the Advisor books the Embassy appointment, sources the interpreter, attends the Prefettura or acts as a representative: none of that is in brand-facts. If the writer wants to say it, use [[VERIFY: does Wedded Concierge book the Nulla Osta appointment, source the interpreter and attend the Prefettura and comune with the couple?]].

must_fix.issue: 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms...' appears 10 times, almost once per section. Readers call it a template and a sales hook: 'I lost count after about eight', 'by the tenth time it sounds like a template', 'by the fifth time it feels like a sales nudge'.
must_fix.fix: Keep it in 2 to 3 places where it carries weight: the Nulla Osta lead time (line 54), civil venue approval (line 145) and the cost section (line 185). Elsewhere end on the plain 'Not published:' line or cut the sentence (lines 27, 72, 112, 149, 163, 173). Keep the 'Not published' wording itself: readers praised the honesty.

must_fix.issue: The close leans on brochure voice: 'stays with you from the first document to the last dance' is flagged as filler or sales talk by four readers, and it is where trust should peak.
must_fix.fix: Make the close quieter and factual: drop 'from the first document to the last dance'; keep 'works in your time zone' and 'quotes in AUD' (see conflicts_resolved); add 'the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins' (brand-facts claim). One CTA, unchanged destination.

should_fix.issue: Australians living outside Australia (Dubai, London, Singapore) cannot tell which office issues their Atto Notorio; every consulate listed is state-based and Melbourne asks for proof of a Victorian or Tasmanian address.
should_fix.fix: Add one or two sentences in the Atto Notorio section using sourced facts only: the Embassy says to get it from the Italian consulate in the state where you reside, and if you cannot get it in Australia, from a Tribunale Civile in Italy or the marriage office of the comune where you marry (fact_04, fact_05); Melbourne asks for proof of a Victorian or Tasmanian address (fact_10). Whether an Italian consulate in another country will issue it for an Australian living there is not in the source pack: write 'not published' (no marker) and, if it fits, fold the Advisor mention into the 2 to 3 allowed. No invented consulate rules.

should_fix.issue: The 10-row, 3-column timeline table needs sideways scrolling on a phone and iPad. It is also the most praised element on the page, so the fix is format, not content.
should_fix.fix: Make it mobile friendly: either a 2-column table ('When' | 'What and where', merging the Where column into the start of the cell in bold) with shorter cells, or move the long sourcing notes (Adelaide, Brisbane, Bagno a Ripoli specifics) out of the cells into a line under the table. Keep every row and every fact comment.

should_fix.issue: The primary persona would not click the CTA because it assumes the couple already has 'your date and your comune'; at 9 to 18 months out they have neither, so the invitation reads as being for couples further along.
should_fix.fix: Reword the CTA lead-in so it welcomes couples without a date or comune, using brand-facts step 1 ('Nothing is too early or too vague'), e.g. 'Speak with a Wedded Advisor about your paperwork timeline, even before you have chosen a date or a town.' Same /wonderland-concierge link with UTM.

consider.issue: Takeaways say what and where but not when to start.
consider.fix: Orchestrator-approved. Swap, do not add (exactly 4 one-sentence takeaways). Merge takeaways 1 and 2 or 3 and 4 to free a slot, then add a sourced 'when' line, e.g. 'Order your certificates and apostilles well before the six-month window opens, because the Atto Notorio cannot be signed earlier than six months before the wedding and DFAT publishes no set turnaround.' (fact_07, fact_24). No month figure that is not sourced.

consider.issue: Privacy: uhnw reads 'publications at the parish and the comune' as names posted publicly and a date leak, with no word on whether notices can be kept discreet.
consider.fix: Only if it fits in one sentence: the source pack shows that where both partners are foreign and neither lives in Italy, comuni such as Bagno a Ripoli use a sworn declaration instead of banns (fact_30), while a Catholic concordat marriage requires publications at the parish and comune (fact_36). What those publications make public is not published: say so, no marker. Do not claim notices can be kept private.

consider.issue: Whether the legal civil ceremony can be held at an exclusive-use private property, and whether a non-Catholic religious ceremony has civil effect.
consider.fix: Venue approval is already 'not published' (line 145); leave it. The non-Catholic religious route is mentioned once (fact_30) and never explained: planner-sme to source it, or the writer adds [[VERIFY: civil effect of non-Catholic religious ceremonies for foreign couples in Italy]] if a sentence is added. Low priority.

consider.issue: Italian terms pile up mid-article (comune, Prefettura, Ufficio Matrimoni, marca da bollo, tabaccaio, NAATI, Prenot@mi); a parent flicks back to remember which office is which.
consider.fix: Optional: gloss Prenot@mi as 'the consulate's online booking portal' and NAATI on first use. No glossary box (word count is already near the top of range).

consider.issue: Examples lean on Bagno a Ripoli; the primary persona has not picked a region and wants a Lake Como or Amalfi comune too.
consider.fix: Only if a comune page is sourced for a Lake Como or Amalfi comune; otherwise add one clause that each comune sets its own rules and Bagno a Ripoli and Montespertoli are worked examples. No invented comune rules.

consider.issue: Primary persona wanted one or two lines on the trade-off of marrying legally in Australia and celebrating in Italy, not just a link.
consider.fix: One sentence of trade-off from sourced facts (fewer steps in Italy; NOIM at least one month before, fact_37). No claim about what 'most couples' choose.

consider.issue: Nulla Osta appointment lead time in Rome or Milan is the most wanted missing number (sceptic, search_visitor, planner_couple).
consider.fix: Not a draft change: it is not published and the draft already says so honestly (readers praised that). Stays on the booking checklist; planner-sme can ask the Embassy (consular-rome@dfat.gov.au) for a refresh. Not classed must-fix because no source exists and the draft handles it per qa-gates.

consider.issue: Funding parent asks about access for older guests at town hall rooms and about travel insurance.
consider.fix: Out of scope for a legal paperwork guide. No change; candidate for a separate guest-logistics post.

keep: The opening correction that British and American guides and a Certificate of No Impediment do not apply to Australians (praised by all five).
The Key takeaways box: 'my answer in the first screen' (search_visitor), screenshot-worthy for partners and parents.
Consulate-by-consulate Atto Notorio detail: Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, including the four unrelated witnesses, the 12-month rule and the Queensland single-status letter.
The direct Embassy quote that Certificates of No Impediment are not valid in Italy, with the Embassy PDF link.
Honest 'Not published:' lines and 'in writing' (trusted by planner_couple, funding_parent, uhnw, sceptic). Trim the Advisor follow-ons, not the 'Not published' statements.
The step-by-step in Italy with real days and hours, and the Prefettura and marca da bollo detail ('nobody would make that up').
The working-back timeline table content and the 'squeeze is in the middle' warning (most useful thing on the page for three readers).
The recognition section, including the surname change catch in NSW and Victoria and the 'in most cases' hedge.
'Works in your time zone' and 'quotes in AUD' in the close (the two most reassuring lines for planner_couple and funding_parent).
The DFAT fees link and payment-method details (cash only in Brisbane, card only at the Embassy).
conflicts_resolved: 'Quotes in AUD' in the close: uhnw says it signals a standard package; planner_couple (primary, weight 0.40) and funding_parent call it one of the two most reassuring lines. Keep it; the brief's reader is a 130k-budget Australian couple, not the UHNW segment.

Tone of the CTA: uhnw wants a discreet private line or referral route; planner_couple wants low pressure and finds the current CTA fine apart from the date/comune assumption. Keep a single public CTA aimed at the primary persona; a private line is deferred (named Advisor/phone line not confirmed).

Fee figures: four readers (all but uhnw) want dollar amounts or a dated range in 'What the paperwork costs', and the source pack holds official figures (DFAT apostille A$105 from 1 January 2026; Sydney Atto Notorio EUR 28; marca da bollo EUR 16; Nulla Osta A$80/A$88/A$90 in conflict). The person chose 'a fee applies' to avoid Nic sign-off. Per orchestrator, this is logged as a human decision (open_questions), not a must-fix, and the writer must not add figures. It is the single biggest drag on enquiry likelihood.

'Your Wedded Advisor confirms' lines: the 'Not published' honesty earns trust across the panel, while the Advisor follow-on erodes it after the third use. Resolution: keep every 'Not published' statement, cut the Advisor follow-on to 2 to 3 instances.

Who does the legwork: uhnw wants it said that a representative handles Rome, the Prefettura and the comune; the source pack says each Australian signs the Nulla Osta in person and the couple attends the Atto Notorio, and brand-facts does not confirm representative services. The writer states what is sourced and what brand-facts allows, nothing more.
deferred_by_person: Wedded Concierge fee amount, fee model and whether commissions or margins are taken (sceptic, funding_parent). Writer may state only the brand-facts claim that the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
Deposits, refunds, contracts, contracts in English and AUD, and who carries the cost if a written confirmation is wrong (funding_parent, sceptic).
'From AUD' price ranges and a rough all-in AUD range for the paperwork (funding_parent, planner_couple, search_visitor, sceptic). Nic signs off any figure.
A named Wedded Advisor, phone line, after-hours on-the-day contact or private referral line (funding_parent, uhnw).
Real weddings: an Australian couple married legally in Italy with venue, comune and date (planner_couple, sceptic); large-scale delivery evidence of 200 to 400 guests with security (uhnw).
Wedded Privileges detail (not raised by readers; listed for completeness, still deferred).
payload.gate_note: Weighted enquiry likelihood 2.0 is well below 3.8 and there are 3 must-fix items, so revise (one round per G6). Not 'stop': the piece meets the brief and all five readers rated relevance and trust well. Caution for the orchestrator: most of the enquiry gap comes from deferred business answers (fee model, named Advisor, real weddings) and the human decision on printing official fees. The copy fixes here should lift trust and the primary persona's click intent, but are unlikely on their own to reach 3.8; G6 should not loop on that.
